en: The Sūtra of the Dhāraṇī of the True and Perfect Meaning of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Noble Eight Thousand Line Prajñāpāramitā,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao Feng Da Fu, Acting Minister of the Court of Imperial Entertainments.
I take refuge in the supreme Mother of all Buddhas, The Dharma of Prajñāpāramitā;
From her are born all Buddhas of the past, future, and present.
The Buddhas who give birth to all goodness are the Mother of Buddhas; The self-nature of non-self-nature is the purity of the self.
The Buddha spoke extensively for Subhūti; Now I have briefly compiled it according to what was said.
The Prajñāpāramitā has one hundred and eight names:
first, the most supreme Prajñāpāramitā; second, omniscience (*sarvajñatā*); third, the knowledge of all aspects (*sarvākārajñatā*);
fourth, the limit of reality (*bhūtakoṭi*); fifth, suchness (*tathatā*); sixth, unalterable suchness (*ananyathā-tathatā*).
7. Unchanging suchness (ananyatathatā), 8. True nature (bhūtatā), 9. Arising as it truly is (yathābhūtotpatti), 10.

7. Like a potter’s wheel, [the hundred and eight names] signify that all phenomena are of one single flavor.
These one hundred and eight names of the Prajñāpāramitā, if constantly maintained and recited, will eliminate all sins and are praised by all Buddhas.
All Bodhisattvas and all worthy sages shall constantly provide protection throughout the long course of time.
Then he spoke the dhāraṇī of the true and perfect meaning of the Prajñāpāramitā, saying:
*Tadyathā* (one phrase).
Oṃ prajñe prajñe mahāprajñe svāhā prajñālokakari.
Añjanavidāmanī svasti susvasti.
